title: Power scaling limits for solar-electric propulsion
bottleneck: Ion and Hall thrusters are extremely propellant-efficient but power-hungry, and their power comes from solar arrays whose output falls with the square of distance from the Sun. Beyond Mars, arrays big enough to drive high-thrust electric propulsion become enormous, heavy, and hard to point — erasing the mass advantage. Nuclear power would solve it, but no flight-ready space reactor in the needed class exists, leaving deep-space electric propulsion starved of energy exactly where it is most valuable.
why_it_blocks: This caps solar-electric propulsion to the inner solar system; outer-planet and interstellar-precursor missions cannot use the most efficient engines available.
current_state: NASA's Psyche mission flies large solar-electric arrays to the asteroid belt; Uranus/Neptune orbiter studies wrestle with power. Nuclear-electric propulsion remains in the study phase.
